The design doc adds a section titled "Tracks and learning path (explainer page only...)" and one titled "No track has dead links", and says "The decisions page gets only the skip link and the shared CSS rules, not tracks or the learning path". findings.summary: The learning path on the published homepage leaves out the job-evidence section.
findings.evidence: build() calls with_evidence(render(..), evidence_section(..)) after finish() has already built the nav. So `<section id="job-evidence">` appears on index.html but not in the learning-path `<ol>`. The test checks render() only, so it does not see this. The design doc says so ("the job-evidence section is inserted after it"), but the CHANGELOG's "a learning-path list of every section" is off by one for the built page. Fix: build the path after the evidence section is inserted, or add an evidence entry to the path.

findings.summary: The core track hides Transitions, the study's main content.
findings.evidence: EXPERT_SECTIONS = ["Counters", "Transitions"]. A newcomer on the default track sees no transition cards, though Start here says it follows one piece of work. No link breaks, and the test proves that. Whether Transitions belongs in the core track is a content choice worth a reader check under the outcome-check default.

findings.summary: The test models the core track with string surgery, not by applying the CSS.
findings.evidence: without_expert removes from each class="expert" match to the first matching close tag, which would mis-cut nested elements of the same name. It is adequate for today's flat sections and li elements, and the CSS rules it relies on are asserted directly.

summary: The change does what the retry asked, and I judge it a pass. The explainer page now has a skip link, a core/expert track switch done in CSS alone, a learning-path list that includes sections with ids, focus-visible outlines and a reduced-motion rule. The viewport and dark-mode rules are kept. Only Counters and Transitions are marked expert. The claims section, the glossary and the next steps stay in every track, so the dead claim links from the earlier attempt are gone. I ran `cargo test -p xtask site` here and all 38 tests pass, including the two new ones. The first new test renders the real page, checks every in-page link in both tracks, checks that the named sections are visible and checks that each feature exists. The second shows that marking the claims section expert would be caught. The decisions page gets only the skip link and the shared styles, and the docs say exactly that. The spec entry OLY-B-D2-02 now names site.rs and that test, ending `status: not shown`. For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I relied on Athena's recorded CI results, which passed; I did not rerun them. Three things are worth fixing later but do not block. The published homepage adds the job-evidence section after the learning path is built, so the path leaves it out. Hiding Transitions by default may be too much for a newcomer. The test removes expert sections by cutting text from the HTML, which works for today's flat structure but would misjudge nested elements.
